Oriel College Faces Calls to Cancel Student Reform Group Event Featuring Nathan Cofnas

28 Oct 2026, 08:26 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Education Desk · Source: www.theguardian.com

Image: www.theguardian.com — Creative Commons

Key takeaways Overview of the Controversy at Oxford Oxford University’s Oriel College is facing mounting pressure from campaign groups, academics, alumni, and members of the public to cancel an upcoming student-organized event. The controversy centers on an appearance by Nathan Cof

Overview of the Controversy at Oxford

Oxford University’s Oriel College is facing mounting pressure from campaign groups, academics, alumni, and members of the public to cancel an upcoming student-organized event. The controversy centers on an appearance by Nathan Cofnas, a blogger and academic who is scheduled to speak at Oriel's Harris lecture theatre on November 17, 2026. The event, titled “An evening with Nathan Cofnas: Is DEI undermining higher education?”, has been organized by Oxon Universities’ Reform Society (OURS), a student group established this year to support Reform UK.

Cofnas previously drew intense media scrutiny after making unproven accusations of plagiarism against Jason Arday, a prominent University of Cambridge professor who resigned from his post and was later found dead in August at the age of 41. Critics argue that Cofnas's past online writings, which have been accused of promoting pseudoscientific ideas regarding racial difference, played a significant role in the intense scrutiny Arday faced before his death.

Open Letter and Campus Reactions

In response to the scheduled November event, an open letter has been circulated and signed by British academics, Oxford alumni, and local campaign groups. The signatories are urging Oriel College to withdraw its facilities from the event, arguing that it risks creating a hostile and exclusionary environment for students—particularly those from ethnic minority backgrounds. Furthermore, critics suggest the booking undermines the college's standing during the year marking the 700th anniversary of its royal charter.

Kehinde Andrews, the UK’s first professor of Black studies, who previously described the media coverage targeting Arday as a coordinated smear campaign, strongly condemned the upcoming Oriel event on social media as “despicable and disgusting.”

Official Responses and Free Speech Obligations

Oriel College issued a formal statement emphasizing its legal responsibilities. The institution stated that it is committed to upholding freedom of speech within the law, noting a statutory duty to protect the expression of views that some may find deeply offensive, while simultaneously maintaining an environment free from discrimination and harassment.

The college clarified that events booked by committee members of registered student societies are evaluated through a code of practice on freedom of speech. Oriel stressed that permitting such an event does not signify institutional endorsement of the speaker's views, and added that security implications and member safety are taken seriously during the booking review process.

Meanwhile, the Oxon Universities’ Reform Society defended the booking. In a public statement and posts on social media, OURS stated that as a registered student society, constituent colleges have a legal obligation to host their events. The student group asserted that the decision to host Cofnas was made exclusively by its committee, maintaining that the event aims to facilitate respectful dialogue on diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI), while also highlighting that the organizers and speaker have faced online hostility.

Practical Implications and Reader Verification

Readers seeking to verify the factual basis of this report, understand the regulatory framework governing UK university free speech, or read the complete statements from Oriel College and student organizers can consult the original reporting by The Guardian at The Guardian.

Confirmed Facts vs. Unknowns

  • Confirmed: Nathan Cofnas is scheduled to speak at Oriel's Harris lecture theatre on November 17, 2026, at an event organized by the Oxon Universities’ Reform Society.
  • Confirmed: Oriel College has received an open letter urging the cancellation of the event, and the college has cited statutory duties regarding freedom of speech.
  • Unknown: The final outcome of the petition, specific security protocols, and attendance figures for the scheduled evening remain undetermined.
